column2: The locket needs a 2×2 space. Existing items are preserved; move it into room and its shape will be updated.
Each item is priced separately. Bargain or pass; we can still talk.
Leave the order. I'll see what I can prepare.
That's the business noted. There's something just for you, too.
That's the budget spent. Everything collected is paid for. I'll find another way to source the rest.
Here for the tools-and-materials order. I've collected {0} tools and {1} materials; {2} credits remain. Show me what you have. We settle each purchase as we go.
I'll pass this time. Don't let me hold up your search.
That's everything. Goods collected, accounts settled. Don't look so surprised. I really did come to give you some business.
The tools-and-materials order has closed. Delivered goods were paid for; the remaining supplies will be sourced elsewhere.
Mother asked me to bring a small request too. Decide whether you want it. Don't say yes just because I brought it.

Two working tools and one ordinary material item. Six hundred in buying funds; we'll inspect and price the goods together. I'll come in two days. If you're short then, you've another four days. Don't empty your own shelves for it.
I'll take these. I'll ask about the rest in two days. Don't buy bad goods just to finish the order.
Interested in the order?

2 tool items and 1 material item. Total buying funds: 600; prices negotiated and paid on delivery. Due four days after the first collection visit. Declining or missing it does not change the relationship or rescue.
Proper business today. They need tools, materials and household goods upstairs. I'm buying for them, with nine hundred to spend. Goods first. I'll tell you about the launch afterwards.
Some people near the ration station pooled money for tools and household goods. Quote normally. Don't give up your margin just because it's me.
All right, that's enough for today. The shop keeps opening; I keep getting on with life. We can deal with Wilde when we're ready.
Two items. My own goods; separate payment. Look them over. I promise the labels survived this time.
Keep it safe. And don't put that one on today's bill.
A sample from Eleanor's first order. Tip, grip and provenance checked. Already covered by the preparations; no further charge.
I'll keep the sample for you. Not taking stock doesn't stop me delivering my own order.
You haven't taken that sample yet. Room on the counter today? It's free. Don't start bargaining with me again.
Let's see the materials.
No stock this time. Tell me about upstairs.
I asked about two small lots on the way: tools or materials. Didn't commit you to either. Want a look? The pass and clothes are paid for. These goods are a separate purchase.
Which lot this time?
The lot you chose is still here. Don't rush. It hasn't grown legs.
Show me the tools.
Here. Look them over. We can take our time with the price.
Take the crate and put it on the counter.
You can inspect it later, or hand it to her directly.
Accept it.
She has started noticing what you need. If there is no room, you can choose again.
Take it, but inspect the crate first.
The stolen-goods record will show up. It may also draw attention.
Come whenever you want. Don't treat yourself like a customer.
I don't need a reason to come.
Get your life steady first. Come or don't—it's fine.
I'll take them. It's compensation for the negotiation.
Taking the money doesn't mean you've priced her mother.
Give it to you and your mother for living costs.
You don't keep the money; it should go to the people who need it.
I won't take it.
You don't want this to look like a sale.
I care about you. But not that way.
Friends route; the rescue is not undone.
I want to know you better. Can we take it slower?
No affection penalty; one more confirmation later.
I like you too. It has nothing to do with where you used to live.
Accept her feelings clearly.
You keep it. It is safer with you.
She holds the drive; you cannot sell it behind her back.
This is too much. I can't be involved anymore.
The line ends here. She will not trust you with anything important again.
Leave it with me. No one takes it without asking you first.
You become the custodian; only you can hand it over.
I want you to come here as more than a regular.
Confirm the 'slower' answer from before.
I've thought it through. Let's stay friends.
Choose friendship, ending the deferred romance decision.
Take the pheromone perfume.
An upper-district item. It might fetch a good price down here.
Take the portable water purifier.
She insists on thanking you. This one will last a while.
Do not mention the crate yet.
She will not know the danger; the trap remains armed.
Keep it. You need it more.
She still has an investigator to pay. Remember the thought.
Pay the normal price (20 credits).
Pay 20 credits rather than turn her gift into another debt. No charge if it cannot be placed; you can choose again.
Use the slower ordinary review (cost {0} credits)
Requires a record from successfully exposing the fake uncle.
If it cannot be done, switch to the exchange.
Keeping her mother alive comes first.
Use a Security review and temporary custody (Security rep {0}+, cost {1} credits)
Requires an existing frame-up or threat record.
Ask the upper district for named sponsorship (Upper District rep {0}+, cost {1} credits)
Trade the work log for acceptance. This is not buying a verdict.
Refuse and let him take it away.
If she never receives it, the trap cannot spring.
Keep it and sell it.
She is still saving for the investigator.
It looks better on you. I'll take the thought.
The locket stays with her.
Go back and raise the money. Return tomorrow.
She is still inside. You are not done trying.
Bring your mother back first. Return the research.
An exchange. Mother and daughter can reunite below, but the research is not published.
Secure the transfer and protection first. Decide who receives the research after she is safe.
Requires admissible material and a channel that actually responds.
Publish the research now.
She takes part in the decision, but no one can promise her mother will live.
This is too much. I'm stepping away.
A normal exit; she handles the rest herself.
Let her finish the investigation herself.
She earned the money. The decision is hers too.
Offer money in exchange for control (cost {0} credits)
She will refuse. Some things are not debts.
Give the drive to a newspaper without telling her.
You make this decision for her, behind her back.
Then I'll keep it.
Accept her gift.
Tell her about the crate.
Let her know it was reported stolen, and not to touch it.
Hand him the drive and take the three hundred (+{0})
Deciding behind her back puts a price on her mother. The relationship ends.
Just make him leave.
Remember the offer and tell her next time. The threat remains.
Hand the record to Security (Security rep {0}+)
Requires an existing frame-up or threat record, and a channel that actually responds.
Sell the drive to a black-market buyer (+{0})
They promise nothing about her mother. The research leaves both your hands.
Ask the upper district to make contact (Upper District rep {0}+)
Trade the research work log for a verifiable response.

The continuing supply contracts are settled too. From tomorrow your share is 600 credits a day. The earlier accounts still stand. Don't call it paying back my wages. This is business we built together.

Once the first order is settled, a share goes to you. From tomorrow, I'll set aside 200 credits a day and bring it when I visit. Missing a visit won't lose you anything. Your capital and the goods we checked together are part of this business.
After the business opens, daily dividends rise to 600 credits, paid during visits.
After the first order succeeds, 200 credits accrue daily, paid during Eleanor's visits.
Here's your share: {0} credits. Everything set aside up to today. Count it. Don't look at me like that. My accounts aren't missing a line.
Keep it safe. I'll keep recording the rest and settle it next time I come.
Eleanor's dividend received: {0} credits. Still awaiting collection: {1}.
Dividends: {0}/day; awaiting collection {1}; received in total {2}.
Brought the accounts. Let's check these entries first. We can talk goods afterwards.
Lydia said you can find a portable water purifier. Budget {0} credits, at least {1} durability. Show me the item first; we'll negotiate the price normally.

Enter Eleanor and Lydia's three-way relationship expansion while keeping the original romance requirements. Progress at 30/60/90 Upper Level reputation and earn three showcase ornaments. No reputation is spent; keep trading and receiving visits while waiting.
Then teach me a few lines.
Continue the original ordinary romance route; this expansion does not begin. Refusal does not lower affection.
I want to tell her how I feel myself.
(Say it) I like you.
(Be clear) I care about you, but let's stay friends.
Think your own business through first.
Sure. Let's look at today's stock first.
Yes. Don't only bring problems—anything you want to say is fine.
It suits you.
Sit down and rest first. The stock won't run away.
You spent all morning working for someone else. Someone should compliment you too.
Changes only this response, not the relationship progression. All three still need to speak for themselves.
I think Eleanor has one just like it.
Changes only this response, not the relationship progression. All three still need to speak for themselves.
It suits you.
Open the explicit three-way discussion; nothing is committed yet.
I like you too. But I'm with her, and I won't promise you anything behind her back. I'll tell her this myself.
You picked the shortest possible confession?
I care about you. Let me sort out what to say first.
Continue the three-way discussion; nothing is committed yet.
I won't promise you anything behind her back. We'll each speak to her ourselves.
I like you too.
Take responsibility and continue the three-way discussion.
I will keep my promises to both of you.
Continue the joint discussion; the relationship is not registered yet.
All right. After you two talk. Whatever you want to ask me, I'll answer.
Commit the dual relationship after both explicit agreements; no fee.
If you're both willing too, then starting today, let's be serious about this—all three of us.
Come here. Let me hold you for a while.
Sit closer. Let's take our time talking today.
I have been keeping this for you: {0}. Have you made room this time?
So this is what you look like. She described you completely wrong.
Want to hear what she said? Not telling. You'd get smug.
She used to ask me which dress to wear before going out. Now she won't even take the job I found her.
...Never mind. I'll tell her that myself.
The goods really are for sale. I also wanted to see whether you'd take a bargain that walked in the door.
Done. Don't tell her about this. She'd definitely call me a busybody.
I've seen that pattern on her bracelet box in upper-district catalogs.
It's her family's. They're one of the upper-district houses selling household goods, perfume and fabric.
When she was little, shop assistants asked whether she liked something before she even looked at the price. Here, she wanted to see what happens when no one flatters her.
Her family sells perfume and bedding. They can't influence the courts. All she can do is come down every few days to see me. Of all her friends upstairs, she's the only one left.
She cares. She just always wants to pick the whole road for me.
Good! Rule one: if she isn't in a hurry to leave, whatever you do, don't ask 'What else do you have?' Just say—your hair clip looks nice today.
If she's not wearing a hairpin, compliment something else! The hairpin isn't the point. Look at her, not just the counter.
That's all I've prepared. They all work! Don't laugh. Thank me after you use them.
Fine, I'll stay out of it. ...But if she asks, I'll say you finally said something decent today.
One more thing. She mentions you more than she mentions today's earnings. I assume most of it is complaining.
She can't admit she misses you every time she sees me.
If she knew I came here, she'd kill me. So I'll say it straight: if you really like her, I can give you a hand.
Because she's my friend. And because every time she tells me what you two talked about, it ends up being about prices! I get anxious just listening.
No tests today. I came to say thanks.
After her mother came back, she finally let herself sleep. When I went to see her the day before yesterday, she'd slept until noon.
I used to tell her to go upstairs and ask old connections to fix it. She wouldn't listen, and I got angry with her.
When she was at her worst, I was still telling her which dress would look more spirited. ...I wasn't hearing a word she said.
I told her. She cursed me out, then asked whether I'd eaten. I suppose that means she forgave me.
She said she wants to help you find customers. When she gets enthusiastic, she runs ahead.
Just tell her clearly how far you can go.
That will do for today.
Lydia came by, didn't she? Did she teach you that?
A few lines. But asking you to stay longer was my own idea. You look... well today.
I slept three hours last night.
She really will teach you anything! ...That's more like it.
My mother complains I put everything away too neatly and now she can't find anything. She shooed me out and told me to find something of my own to do.
To sell goods! ...And to sit for a while.
That plaque... she gave you that too? She can praise a shop she likes for ages, but she rarely puts her own name out there.
She said she'd help you bring in customers. If you want to thank her, do it yourself. Don't route everything through me.
I saw an old brooch. The dealer says a famous person wore it, but I just like the petals. Is the extra price worth it?
It's still in the shop. I haven't paid. Don't laugh at me for buying things just because they look good.
Looking good is a reason. If someone famous wore it, make them show proof. If you like the petals, negotiate the price of the petals.
So it's not that I don't appreciate it - I just don't have to pay for the story too?
I thought you'd say this kind of thing is useless.
Eat something proper first. A piece of cake later doesn't count as lunch.
...I came to teach you how to care about her, and you practiced on me first. Fine, I won't pass that part on.
You can bring your own problems to me too.
I'm not asking about her today. I have something of my own I can't decide on.
Back to you. She hates being left to guess. When the time comes to speak, don't wait for her to ask, and don't start by worrying she'll laugh at you.
You're taking this seriously.
I only teach this much. What you say to her, you'll have to come up with yourself. Don't recite my lines—she'll know.
Speaking of the brooch—do you have anything here that goes with it? Show me.
Look first. The price is the price.
I like you. I don't want to be just the shopkeeper you come to when something's wrong. I won't make you guess anymore.
...Did she teach you that too?
She only taught me to say it clearly. Who I like doesn't need her teaching.
...Me too. I like you! Did you hear me?
There's still dust on my hand.
Should I let go?
Who told you to let go?
...I understand.
We'll keep doing business. Don't start avoiding me just because we've had this talk.
Lydia brings you up every time I see her lately. She says I should hear you out instead of shutting you down with prices.
Everyone I see lately asks what I'm going to do next.
Live a good life. Find proper work, look after Mother. ...And sometimes, I want to come here. Don't make me spell out every word!
She really thinks I can't tell. ...Move your cup this way. It's in the way there.
Which baker made this bread? It's not the one I know, so I'm not buying it.
Do it again. He missed it.
Oh! I promised to look at clothes with someone. Take your time—no need to see me out.
Did you not just say that shop was closing early today?
...There is another one! Just enjoy yourselves!
Your shawl! You forgot it again.
Do not spend the whole time talking about stock.
I booked a table for three. She's been too busy to eat lately, so I'm dragging her out. Of course I'm coming too—otherwise you two would stare at each other and who'd start the conversation?
You two didn't spend the whole time talking about goods afterward, did you? I went to trouble to clear the space. I wasn't doing it for your entertainment.
I'd say I helped. Next time she complains about you, I only need to hear half of it.
She even handed me my shawl that day. ...She always remembers things like that.
I bought that brooch last time! He couldn't prove anyone famous wore it, so I negotiated on the piece itself and got a good discount. It goes with two of my dresses. Both look good.
It's not that one word from you made me stop liking it... It's just that now I can like it without worrying about being fleeced.
From now on, I can ask you about my own things too, right? Next time I'll bring my own problems. Don't get annoyed!
...Fine. I'll think my own business through first.
You really know how to kill the mood. Fine, let's look at the stock.
...I'll hold you to that.
By the way, those two dresses still need something to go with them. What have you taken in lately?
Look for yourself. We'll talk price if you find something.
Anyway, this time I'm going up there as someone who doesn't just have everything handled for her.
Lydia found me a trading house that handles household goods and growing equipment. They need someone to organize delivery records and check stock.
I tried it for two days. The first day they only let me count against the list. Then I caught a crate with the wrong model number, and they let me keep the books myself.
They did! My employer is arranging a work pass for me. I'll run between both levels for now, and once I know the place better, I'll find a room upstairs.
Mother stays below, doing the work she has now. Her restrictions are still there. My having a job doesn't mean her case is closed.
The research office asked me to organize handover records. Some of it has to be done upstairs, with a separate work pass.
I want to go. There's still a lot I don't understand, so I'll do what I can first. Lydia asked about a room I can stay in short-term, not far from there.
Then I'll have to look forward to you getting off work. Set the time aside in advance. You make time, and so do I.
...Why have you not asked whether I will still come?
I was about to ask you out.
...I will. I just cannot run down here with a bag of stock every time I think of you.
Lydia even told me to say it slowly, so you wouldn't think I was leaving.
Does she think we're that bad at talking to each other?
...Sometimes she's not wrong.
My mother's official result came through too. She'll decide about the research and where to live herself. I'll focus on doing my job well first.
Mother's review isn't finished. She lives under her current registration. My getting a pass doesn't mean she'll suddenly move upstairs.
I'm borrowing your place to rest my feet! I spent all morning rearranging a jewelry shop's display. My legs are sore.

The first time, I packed all the brightest pieces together. From a distance you couldn't see anything. Then I left some space, and even the plainest piece got questions. The owner wants me to do it again.
Look here. The petals aren't even the same color.
That is much better than praising how I arrange a display.
You do know how to be thoughtful.
...Why are you so good at talking today?
Good—show me what you've taken in lately. My legs are resting; my eyes aren't.
Tell me which one you want, then we'll talk price.
No rush. I meant to go see the new dresses, but halfway there I came around to this place instead.
The dresses will not run away. Today I came to see whether you had learned to give a compliment—and it seems you have.
Next time you see her, don't keep asking whether work's going well. Sometimes she wants you to notice her new hair ornament.
You changed yours too. You taught me to look at the person, not just the counter. It works.
...You—why are you looking so closely? I told you to look at her!
...Thank you.
...I gave her that one! Is your eye for detail good or bad?
Since I'm already at the counter, show me what you've recently taken in. Don't fob me off with just the most expensive piece.
You can look. Whether you buy is up to you.
There are two days next week when I can come down early. I wrote them down.
When things get busy upstairs, everyone says 'this will only take a moment.' If I don't set time aside in advance, my own plans always get pushed back.
Those two days are ours. Remember that.
Has Lydia been by lately?
She came a few days ago. Then she stopped.
She says she's busy. I mentioned that new shop she's been wanting to visit. She didn't even ask where it was. Just said she'd made other plans.
When she really doesn't want to go out, she complains her shoes pinch or her dress doesn't fit. She wouldn't say she's busy without even hearing where.
Does she talk about her own things when she's here?
She does.
...Before, whenever she talked about you, it was all 'he should do this' and 'you should do that.' Lately she doesn't say a word.
I haven't decided what to ask her yet. And don't suddenly pretend you don't know her just because I asked. That would look worse.
The customer business stays as usual. Whatever's already arranged, I'll make clear.
I didn't ask about customers. These past few days you didn't come, I kept looking at the door.
...I know. Hearing you say that makes it even harder to leave.
From now on, if you want to ask her out, just ask her. I've been... busy lately.
We've already talked directly.
Good. Then my job here is done.
It's not like I have to come around here every day. Last time I came this way, I missed a dress I wanted to see.
...I had other plans later.
If you don't want to talk about it, fine. Don't fob me off with something else.
I thought I'd be happy once it worked out. Happy for her, and happy for you.
It's just... when she told me you'd met, the first thing I thought about was what you talked about. She didn't mention me, and then I was angry at myself for caring.
Don't comfort me. When you look at me seriously, I can't finish a sentence.
Let me think on my own. That's enough for today.
...Then tell her. Every time I think of how she will look at me, I lose all my words.
Honestly... now it's my turn to wait for you to say it clearly. Until you do, don't make me wait in secret. I'll go see her myself too.
I'm not saying I was just passing by this time. I like you.
At first, I just wanted things to go better for her.
You remembered my brooch, and you listened to all those little things. I started looking forward to coming here—and then feared you only asked how she was.
But Eleanor doesn't know yet. You have to tell her the truth. What do you actually want? Don't leave us both guessing.
I was afraid a longer one would make you shut me down with prices again.
All right. I'm not asking you to decide today.
...You—don't answer so fast. Hear me out first.
Lydia says she likes me. I like her too. I don't want to lie and say she's just a friend. I had to tell you myself.
...And then? You really dare say it to my face!
Of course I'm angry! ...I've felt something was off for a while. She didn't come, and you didn't mention her. I thought I was imagining things.
Whenever I asked about her, you changed the subject. You knew you should have told me earlier!
So what do you want now? To break up with me?
I want to be with you. And I have fallen for her too. I owe you both truths, to your face.
...You're honest, at least. What about her? What did she say?
She said she'd come find you herself.
She'll find me?

A couple of days ago I was still thinking that if she never came again, maybe I could pretend none of it happened. Then I wanted to go find her myself. To ask what she was hiding... and afraid she'd actually tell me.
At dinner she held up that bread and imitated a customer. I nearly spilled my water laughing. When she came back for her shawl, I wanted to ask her to sit down again.
I have imagined more evenings together like that. I want you, and I want her to stay too. ...Do not think that means I have stopped being jealous.
After you two talk, I'll still be here.
Let me talk to her first. I have questions for her that you can't answer for me.
Don't suddenly stop coming to see me these next few days. Don't think that because I'm angry, you should stay away.
I'll open as usual tomorrow. If you come, you'll see me.
...Hmph.
I went to find her. ...No, she came to find me first.
The moment she walked in she asked, 'Didn't you say if you like someone, don't make them guess?' That's what I taught her! She used it to shut me up.
I said that was about her. She said: 'So it doesn't count when it's your turn?'
I said if she didn't want to see me again, I just wouldn't—before I finished, she cut in: 'See? Answering for me again.'
I used to watch you two refuse to open your mouths and want to say it for you. Now it's my turn, and I don't even know where to start.
Then she asked what I actually wanted. I said I wanted to see you. Not to walk you to the door and stand outside waiting.
She said she wants the three of us to be like that day again, talking until we lose track of time. She won't stop minding all at once, and she won't give me every agreed evening either.
I said we'd make separate plans. When we go shopping together, she has to finish the trip with me. Don't keep thinking about coming back to see you.
Then we both cried. ...She won't admit it. Don't ask her.
She said she'd come with me next time. I've already thought about what to wear, but the words are still fighting in my head.
Then I will say the most important bit first. I want to be with you.
Me too.
Then it'll be your turn next time. Think before you speak. Don't just sit there saying, 'Whatever you want.'
I want this. ...Give me your hand.
I'm willing too. This time don't leave me at the door.
I only came to help out a little.
You certainly helped thoroughly.
Then I'm charging a referral fee. One kiss... not in front of the whole shop.
Can't you slow down?
Well, you can teach me that later.
She told you I cried, didn't she? She cried first.
I was the one who got out a handkerchief first! ...Oh, never mind. We can argue about that later.
I have thought it over. I want to try this, the three of us. And I will tell you when I am jealous. Do not expect sudden generosity.
And when you ask me out, you cannot spend the whole time looking at her.
You've made plans with her too. I know. Don't keep checking the time today and making me feel I'll have to leave first.
Today's time is yours.
...Kiss me again.
...So when it actually happens, I'm not that good with words after all.
I spent a long time in front of the mirror. If you say nothing, I shall have to compliment myself.
I see. You look beautiful today.
...I thought I'd have to remind you.
Finished yet? I spent ages choosing what to wear, and that is all the attention I get?
...How long do you want me to stay today?
I missed you.
Where are we going today? We're already here.

Mm. I picked it for this place. I tried one on first, but it looked too much like meeting a relative. Then I changed to this one and couldn't give up the color of the other. I turned in front of the mirror for ages.
You chose well. You don't need lessons now.
When I was teaching you to compliment her, I never thought one sentence could be so hard to answer. ...Then look a little longer. It's not just for the glance at the door.
Do you remember the display I arranged for the jewelry shop? The owner came to me again. I want to try a different layout this time.
Today is our agreed time. I just want to hear you say it once.
Work's fine. Everyone upstairs knows which day I leave early. I told them I'm coming to see you - no sneaking around.
...Last time it was her turn to keep you company, right? I won't ask how long. I'm a little jealous! Don't laugh. I just want to know.
Don't recite everything you said to her the moment you see me. It makes me feel like I'm here to audit the books.
I only want to say one thing today—when I come back from upstairs, the first person I want to see is still you. Don't think one more person means I'll ask for less.
I wasn't planning to ask you to.
Then hold me tighter.
Don't say 'let's just eat something' today.
If we don't plan it, someone always ends up busy until the food's cold and calls it dinner.
She means you, and herself too.
Now you're finishing my sentences for me?
You used to finish mine more than I do yours.
Then I'll just—
Sit down. You don't have to make room for us today.
I didn't say I was leaving. It's just... last time I sat here, at this point I'd be finding an excuse.
You don't need one this time. Your portion is still here.
...Then I won't go. We haven't had the pastries yet.
This dessert wasn't bought especially for us, was it?
It was at first. Today I wanted some too. I'm usually direct. Only liking you took a little practice.
Let me try yours too. Hers has even more cream than mine.
All that choosing, and you still want someone else's.
You just took something from his bowl!
The plaque is still up. Business, like I said, depends on you.
So are you here to inspect the business today?
Not today. Both the people I wanted to see are here.
Both of you sit closer. I don't want to look at you across the table.
Gladly! Move this way. I saved you some dessert.
Any closer and there will be no room left on my side.
And you have the nerve to say that about me?
Help me choose. Does this shawl suit the dress, or was the other one better?
You asked me three times on the way here.
That's why I'm asking him. Come on, don't look at the books first.
This one. ...You changed too? Both look good. Stand closer.
Mm. Closer it is.
Someone praised you at dinner tonight. She said the old clock she bought here kept better time than her new one.
Are you going to ask again whether I told people I found this shop first? I was too busy being happy to remember!
Then stay with me a little longer. Call it celebrating for me.
Gladly. But first, have a look at these earrings.
Since I've shown you mine, bring out what you've taken in lately. An ear clip needs something to go with it.
Pick something. The price is the price.
She asked me to tell you she'll come later.
Right now is mine. The second half was my addition. Don't cut it.
The two of us are going out tomorrow. Remember to eat.
Who complained last time that we took too long shopping? You're not coming this time.
Then bring back something good to eat.
That's easy!
Someone outside was staring at my name earlier. They didn't come in. First they asked whether I was really me.
What did you say?
I said yes, then told him to look at the goods, not just at me.
You're getting better at business.

I'm Eleanor. You'll see my mother's name in the news soon enough.
I can't believe I'm stuck in a place like this.
No word from my mother, and they won't let me back upstairs.
sighs Do you have household goods?
Looks like I'll be here for a while. I need a cup, something to clean with, and a decent lamp.
I found a room across from the ration station. It's small, but at least it doesn't stink.
This cup has a chip in it.
The intact one is over there. It's not like I can't afford it.
...I'll take the cheap one. The chip isn't on the side I drink from.
My roommate says fix the lock first, worry about curtains later.
She also says the perfume I brought would cover half a month's rent.
Upper-district custom. The cap's loose. Half a bottle left. You won't see one down here twice a year.
...Hmph.
Same price you quoted. Fine, I'll take these.
Cheaper again?
Do you do this for every customer?
...I'll take it.
The same goods cost more here than anywhere else?
This is my first time living in the lower levels. It doesn't mean I can't do arithmetic!
Forget it. I'll look around. There must be more than one shop down here.
The neighbours argue every night. It sounds like they're right next to my bed.
That racket saves me buying a radio.
...That joke was terrible.
I can't believe people spend their whole lives in a place like this.
Hey. Me again.
My funds are running low. They didn't let me bring much with me.
If I could get back upstairs, I could explain everything and clear our name.
Everything could go back to normal, and I wouldn't have to eat Nutrifruit every meal.
Anyway, I brought some of my own things to sell. Bottled water, toiletries, and perfume.
Careful with that. The perfume cap is loose.
Down here, there's no need to smell like you're going to a banquet.
You won't see bottles like this in the lower levels twice a year.
Then keep counting. Do you really need to price every single thing?
Lately, people who price by my name won't offer a single credit.
...I don't have any other family. Just my mother.
Less than I thought. But the price is fair.
Fine. That price.
That's higher than I expected.
It'd better be useful. Don't let me come back and find them still here, like they're waiting for pity.
You know what it's worth. You also know I'm short on money.
...Fine. Today you caught me at a bad time.
Fine, I'll take them. If you won't buy, someone else will.
There's also this. My mother gave it to me.
...Ask me for a price first. I haven't decided.
I'm not selling this today.
This is mine. I'll bring it out when I've decided.
Hello there. You know Eleanor, don't you? I'm her... uncle.
We prepared a little gift for her. Only the best from the upper district.
But I can't find her anywhere.
Young people get upset and hide. I hear she comes here often.
Next time she visits, could you give this to her?
Make sure it reaches her hands. Not yours. Hers.
If anyone asks, you never saw me.
Oh, and keep Security out of this. It's a family matter.
Good. Put it in her hands, not yours. I'll know.
Hello, shopkeeper. You reported stolen goods?
I didn't steal it! I have the receipt right here.
Then why did you report it as stolen?
Filing a false theft report is a crime. Come along quietly.
You run a shop, boss. Mind your own counter.
Someone tampered with my counter. That makes it my business.
*tells her about the man claiming to be her uncle*
My uncle? I don't have an uncle.
I told you. Apart from my mother, I don't have any family.
The crate was reported stolen. He's the one who reported it.
He left me a crate? One that was reported stolen?
They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
The crate was reported stolen, and it's still in my storeroom. Don't touch it.
A 'gift' that was reported stolen... They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
I didn't take it. He couldn't explain where it came from.
...Thank you for telling me.
If anyone else claims to be my family, throw him out.
My mother is already locked up. Isn't that enough for them?
I... I need to think.
Before, if someone sent me a crate like that, I wouldn't even check the label. I'd just open it.
Now I know. Nothing in the lower levels comes free. Not upstairs either.
You warned me. Take this. It's the last thing I brought from home.
I'll come back when I've sorted out my thoughts.
I can't take it anymore.
My money's gone. Someone broke in last night and took what was left.
Only this locket survived. I was wearing it.
I wasn't there. My roommate went to ask around. No word yet.
The verdict came down too. They found my mother guilty.
I don't know what to do. I'll be stuck down here, and she'll rot in that cell.
I kept thinking about how I'd explain to her that I sold everything we brought from home.
Now... I don't even have the chance to explain.
I can't believe I'm asking this.
But could you spare some food? Anything edible. Please.
Thank you. I won't forget this.
That's enough. Really. Don't bring out any more.
My roommate split her share with me yesterday.
The first day I came here, I called you frogs in a well. I said people down here live like this their whole lives.
...I'm sorry. Those things I said were wrong.
...I can see the shelves.
If you ever get more stock, could you save me a little? Just a little.
...I understand. You run a shop, not a charity.
When I have money, I'll buy at full price.
Don't tell anyone about today.
Me begging you for food. And me apologising.
Especially the second part!
Don't tell anyone I came here to beg today.
Thank you. There aren't many things I can still decide for myself. Let me keep this one.
Don't move! That crate was reported stolen.
What? It's not mine! I've never seen it before!
Like mother, like daughter. Come with us.
Please, someone set me up! Shopkeeper, tell them!
You're the one who set them straight, aren't you? They rechecked the theft report.
I said it over and over in there. The crate wasn't mine.
One of the officers laughed. He said my mother said the same thing.
I'm out. She's still in there.
You were tricked too. ...But next time, ask me first. All right?
You knew it was reported stolen?
I knew. I messed up.
Then don't act as if getting me out makes it never happen.
I'll write down what you spent on me. I'll pay back every credit.
...If you have anything to eat here, give me some. If not, we'll think of something together.
Hey! I'm back!
After last time, I figured things out. Life goes on. Besides, I'm almost used to the stench.
So I went scavenging at the dump. My roommate gave me a crash course.
I have to admit, there's a real community spirit down here.
Come look at what I found. ...Don't laugh.
I think this one's usable. That one's old, but the inside is fine.
This one's broken here? Then knock the price down. I thought it was just dirt. I spent ages wiping it.
You don't have to say every piece is good just to make me feel better.
Good. You take the goods, I take the credits.
This is much better than standing here waiting for you to pity me.
You paid too much. This lot will sell well, right?
Then you'll have to tell me what it's normally worth. I have to learn.
Is that price because the goods aren't worth much, or because you think I can only sell to you?
It's fine. I'll remember what you don't buy and bring something else next time.
I've been thinking about what to do next.
I'm sure someone in the upper district set up my mother. I can't go up there and ask around, but a private investigator can.
A reliable one costs eight hundred credits.
Eight hundred isn't small. So I'll keep scavenging the dump and selling what I find to you.
Give me a fair price, all right? Every credit gets me closer.
I've asked other buyers too, and I took some short work cleaning grow tanks. I can't rely on your shop alone.
Hey, me again. This is what I found at the dump this time.
I priced it all myself first.
This one's casing is damaged, but the inside is fine; this one looks new, but the connector's rusted, so knock the price down; the last one I'm not sure about.
Better than picking things at random the first time, right?
At the dump today, someone tried to trade me a bag of broken parts for my stuff. Said I clearly didn't know the market.
Of course not! I told him to take it to the pawnshop and let the owner decide what it's worth.
The moment he heard it was your shop, he turned around and left faster than I did.
I didn't expect your shop's name to carry more weight than my family name down here.
...Only when it comes to scrap.
Still better than my name. My name can't even buy scrap now.
He said he'd never heard of any pawnshop, muttered something, and left.
At least I didn't get fooled. That's the important part.
Add today's sale, and we're one step closer to eight hundred.
I've set aside food money. Nutrifruit doesn't feel like punishment every meal now.
...Sometimes it still does.
Now I know that buying what I scavenged at a fair price counts as help too.
Don't tell me again that this is just what the lower levels pay. I've asked other buyers.
It's worth what it's worth. My being desperate doesn't make it cheaper.
Wait. Don't lump this material in with the rest.
...It's for you.
I'm still saving for the detective. This one doesn't change that.
Last time you were buying stock, you looked at this material a little longer. I found it at the dump, so I kept it.
I'm not just standing here waiting to count your money. Don't get the wrong idea. I just have a good eye.
Take it. When you use it later, don't tell people it was just something I picked up.
...Even though I did.
This is something I wanted to give you. If you insist on paying, fine.
But you should know: this time I'm not the one asking you for help.
You won't take it? Fine. Next time I'll pick something you can't find an excuse to refuse.
My roommate asked how I knew you'd be open today.
I said anyone running a proper business opens on time.
Then she asked why I didn't go somewhere else.
I told her to mind her own radio and stop going off in the middle of the night.
What are you laughing at? She really is loud!
I'll slowly pay back what you've done for me.
...This is the last time I'll say it. From now on, just watch what I do.
So this is the shop Eleanor never stops talking about?
She's not here today? I know. I picked a day she'd be out.
Selling. I set the price. You decide whether to take it.
She says you have a sharp eye. I want to see how sharp.
This quality, and you'll pay that? You even noticed the clasp was replaced?
Fine. She wasn't exaggerating.
You took it without arguing.
She said you never take advantage of people. I suppose it depends on whose advantage it is.
You won't buy it? Fine. At least you didn't pretend to know.
She used to buy things based only on whether she liked the look. She never asked the price.
Now she asks more questions than anyone. She told me: when you buy stock, you look at the goods, not who brought them.
Her exact words were much ruder. I picked the part I could repeat.
I can find her a job up there. A place to live too.
I brought it up with her. There's only one condition: stop bringing up her mother's case in public.
She didn't agree. That's my answer.
She keeps saying 'there are people down here too.' I thought she was just being stubborn.
What kind of spell have you people put on her? Nutrifruit?
*snorts* ...No wonder she says you're infuriating.
If she asks, tell her I came to sell something.
...Just don't make me sound better than I am.
Lydia came by.
Brought a bracelet, said she could find me a job upstairs.
There were conditions.
I turned her down. The job itself was fine.
Live in a house someone hands me, learn to keep quiet, and pretend I don't have a mother? I can't do that!
She also said I have a way of needling people. She's not wrong.
She also asked whether you were only interested because I used to have money, waiting for the day I recover so you can cash in.
I said that when everyone else changed their expression the moment they heard my name, you were still looking down at the goods.
When I was at my poorest, you didn't suddenly turn into a different kind of shopkeeper.
I said you've done things that made me furious. But you came back and made them right.
I know what happened better than she does. She doesn't get to decide for me.
I said I'd judge for myself. ...If you really are waiting for me to recover before you start offering fair prices, you'd better stop waiting.
I don't need you to vouch for me. I have faith in my own judgment.
She said I never used to admit I'd misjudged someone.
I admit it now. For example, I used to think everyone down here was the same.
Don't get smug. I'm not right about people every time either.
...You didn't argue.
By the way. Did she also praise your eye for goods?
She praises everyone like that. Don't take it seriously.
...And don't talk to her too long. That mouth of hers could talk anyone in circles.
That's everything sold for today. I'll stay here a while. It's not like I'm here to keep you from making money.
If today's batch sells, it should be enough.
Price it by the goods, not by the number I'm trying to reach. I could say that line for you.
I know exactly how much is missing. If it's not enough, I'll make another run to the dump tomorrow.
I didn't give him all the originals. I kept copies, and noted the time of every meeting.
Thank you. I'm going to find out who did this to my mother.
...Today I was going to say I finally don't have to keep running to your shop.
I didn't say I'd stop coming. Until it's cleared up, I still have to eat.
I can pay. But from now on, you listen to me.
Put the business terms in writing. Whether I take the loan is my decision.
Not just business.
Then no loan.
My mother didn't teach me to pay a debt with myself. That's not how it works down here either.
The money's done. I sold the rest of the goods to another buyer and took an advance on some short work.
Their price wasn't good. I'll have to work a few more days. But I'll manage.
I'll manage. I said I'd find my own way.
The last part of the shortfall, I was planning to cover with the locket.
It's been hanging on me doing nothing. Now I want it to help me find my mother.
I have. Price it like anything else.
Hey. The detective found something.
We changed the handoff location, and no one followed me here.
It's a data drive, hidden in my mother's old lab at the hydroponics farm.
It's password-locked. The detective couldn't open it. But I know the password. Mom always used my birthday.
I warned her many times that it wasn't safe. She always said she was afraid she'd forget when she got busy.
I can't wait any longer. Let's open it here.
*looking at the screen*
This is... genetic research. About Nutrifruit.
She found a way to make ordinary Nutrifruit produce seeds again. Plant it, harvest the fruit, and save your own seeds.
With this data, any decent biohacker could modify it.
No more buying seeds from Pastel. This would cost Pastel dearly.
That's why they went after her.
There are work records here too. Someone ordered her to stop the experiment. A few days later, her access was revoked.
The embezzlement charge is fabricated. All of it. It was orchestrated by Pastel's representative on the station.
My mother is still in their hands. This can't go out yet.
I... I need some time to think about what to do.
Leave it with me. No one takes it without asking you first.
This isn't ordinary storage. All right.
People come and go here every day. It'll be safer with you.
All right. We agree on who it goes to first. No changing our minds at the last minute.
This is too big. I can't be involved anymore.
...I understand. I'll take the drive. Please don't tell anyone what I said today.
That crate last time. Remember me?
Surprised? I'm out again. Someone sorted the paperwork. Some things aren't as hard as you think.
Boss, I have a message. About Eleanor and the research disk she has.
We know you've been in contact with Eleanor, and we know about the data drive.
She's seen what's on it. She knows who we work for.
Tell her to return it, or her mother dies.
Hand it over and we release her mother. She'll be exiled to the lower levels, but she'll live.
Believe it or not. She will.
If you get her to return it, you'll earn three hundred credits.
You run a pawnshop. Why meddle in this?
Someone will handle the release. You don't need to worry about it.
You really plan to see this through for her? ...Don't take too long.
Boss, you'd better think carefully. The record will show your part too.
Then write it all down. Don't just write hers.
Message delivered. Tell her to come talk when she's decided.
*tells her about their offer to release her mother*
If I return the drive, they'll let her go?
Exiled down here... but alive.
He also said I'd get three hundred when it's done.
...You even told me that. Thank you.
But if I go public, they'll kill her. And then no one will need Pastel's seeds again.
I want her to live. I can't pretend to be brave about that.
But the research is real. If I keep a copy and hand it back, they'll still find a way to hurt her.
I don't know what to do. If it were you, what would you do?
Apply for temporary custody first, then talk about reopening the case. The records of the frame-up and threats, plus the research, prove she's in danger and what their motive is.
I'll prepare her identity papers and medical history. I know what medication she used to take.
I don't have a way to get her out right now.
Then we negotiate their release terms first. I can't gamble with my mother's life.
If someone takes over her protection, I want to know who's responsible and when I can see her.
And don't go see that enforcer alone.
I'm already waiting for one person to come out of there. I don't want to wait for another.
Bring your mother back first. Return the research.
You're right. She's my only family.
But I need to see them release her with my own eyes. Not just move her from one cell to another.
Secure the transfer and protection first. Once she's safe, we decide who gets the research.
All right. I'll organize her files. Tell me what you need. Don't finish everything alone and only then tell me.
If we publish it, everyone will know what they did. But I cannot promise your mother will survive.
I know they mean it. ...Give me a moment.
They won't even say where to pick her up. If I hand over the drive and they change the terms, what do I have to bargain with?
I want her back, and I'm afraid they'll erase the research she spent so long on.
...Take it to the newspaper. At least the research will be out there.
Don't wait for word about protection. I don't know if Mother would agree. I can't speak for her without seeing her.
This is my choice. I will take it there today.
But do not tell me this means she will be safe. We both know it does not.
The application's in. Still waiting for an answer.
You didn't tell me 'it's already fine.'
That's better, actually. People used to say 'don't worry' every time, and then I never saw them again.
I'm taking another short shift tonight. Waiting for news doesn't stop me eating.
I told my roommate that if anyone asks where my mother lives, not to say a word.
My roommate says I'm learning this late.
Your part is in the application too.
I checked your shop address twice.
Afraid that if something happens, I wouldn't be able to find you.
You're here. That's why I dared to take it this far.

I... I can see her?
All right. I'll go now. Verify first, then see her.
If it's real, I'll come back and tell you. In person.
Verify the person and the paperwork first. Don't just take a messenger's word that it's done.
I want my mother to confirm it herself. Someone else reading a line for her doesn't count.
No copy. If I'm trading it for her, I can't use her life as collateral and gamble that they won't find out.
I've thought it through. Whether there's another way later is a later problem.
Today, I just want to see her.
Still no confirmation that she can be released, right?
No. Keep applying, or switch to handing over the drive for her release.
I don't want to treat 'processing' as if she's already safe. Get her out first.
Hey! My mother is free!
I saw her myself! The first thing she asked was whether I'd been skipping meals again.
She was exiled to the lower levels. She can't go back to her old farm.
But we're together again. Tonight, I know where she's sleeping.
I saw Mother! She's been moved out, someone's watching over her, and the visit is registered.
She knows what comes next. The research, the threats, going public. I told her everything.
She said to let the protection staff confirm the arrangements first, then send the material out.
She said I'm reckless enough for both of us. Someone in the family has to ask more questions.
I had so much prepared: how she ate in there, why she didn't tell me sooner, whether anyone hurt her.
Not a single one. I just called her 'Mom'.
She said she heard me, and I didn't have to shout.
Now I can ask her slowly.
I used to think that as long as I could get back upstairs, everything would return to the way it was.
But today, when I saw her, I didn't even think about the house up there.
First I'll find a place to live down here. My roommate will help look, and I can keep working.
If I need anything, I'll buy it. At full price. You've done too much for us. I can't have you paying for everything from now on.
But today, I want to thank you properly, once.
All I could say then was that I wanted to save her. You helped me bring her home.

The research on restoring nutrifruit seeds has been handed to independent researchers for verification. The representative of Pastel's station office is suspected of coercion and interference in the case and is now under investigation.
The person concerned is currently under registered protection. The original embezzlement case is still under review; the investigation result does not constitute a final ruling.

The registered protection arrangements have been confirmed. The family is permitted to register a residence in the lower levels and live together, and may carry on normal daily activities. Contact person and address are on file; contact must be maintained during the review of the original case.
Hello. Eleanor says that when you buy things here, the owner tells you the flaws first.
She also said the owner isn't always good with words, but he's not a bad person.
I'd like to buy some household goods. There's still a lot missing where we live.
She's off to work. Before she left, she told me not to lug home everything just because it's cheap.
I used to tell her the same thing, and she'd pretend not to hear.
She told me what you did for her.
But when she talks about herself, she says far less than when she talks about you.
Or maybe she's waiting for me to ask.
The research was returned. Of course that doesn't sit well with me.
But don't let her think bringing me back is something she has to apologize to me for.
The material has been sent out. I'll keep cooperating with the review. The rest will take time, step by step.
You were right to get me transferred before publishing. The people with the least protection shouldn't always be the ones paying the price.
That's all. Don't refuse to take my money just because it's me.
She won't take things for free. That part is certainly like me.
When she talks about this place lately, it's not just about what she bought.
And whatever else she said, go ask her yourself. I won't finish her sentences.
Did my mother come by?
She did. Bought some things, paid for them. She told me to ask you.
I knew it.
Then don't ask today!
I brought some goods. This time I'm really here to sell.
My mother gets up earlier than I do now. Two days ago I woke up and found her sitting there repairing an old tray.
She says if her hands aren't doing something, she starts thinking about what happened in there.
I handed her the tools and sat with her for a while.
Nothing special. I just sat there for a while.
I always thought that once she was out, I'd know what to do next.
Work continues, the room needs tidying, meals have to be made. I know all that.
It's just... I don't need to invent a reason to come here so I can ask you for help.
You don't need a reason to come here.
You said that. Remember it.
You said that. Remember it.
...You've gotten rather direct lately. Fine, I'll remember that.
You're making this easy for me. All right, I'll get my life steady first.
I'll still come to sell goods. You don't have to ask me what happened every time.
I'm a regular. Ordinary customers don't know what you buy.
There's something we need to settle first. I haven't forgotten the crate from the man pretending to be my uncle.
You did make it right afterward, and you've told me things first ever since.
I'm willing to trust you again. But what you did that time was still wrong.
If there's danger from now on, I'll tell you first.
No goods today. There is something I want to tell you.
You always ask what's for sale first. Don't ask today.
I've been coming more often lately than when I had goods to sell.
I wonder whether you found anything good today, whether your lunch has gone cold again, whether you argued with another difficult customer.
Mother is safe now, and I still want to see you every day.
Eleanor, I feel—
Wait. Let me finish. I like you.
There. Your turn. Don't keep me waiting.
I like you too. It has nothing to do with where you used to live.
Nothing to do with where I lived? Easy for you to say.
Then when I needle you, don't dodge.
Good. Then I won't need an excuse to come here anymore.
I want to know you better. But can we take it slowly?
Yes. I'm not asking you to sign a lifetime contract today.
Just don't pretend you didn't hear me.
I care about you. But not that way.
I see.
You telling me directly is better than letting me guess.
You don't owe me for the past. And this isn't repayment.
I'll still come sell goods in a couple of days. Act normal then.
I said some harsh things before. I want to add one thing today.
Thank you for always treating me like someone who can do things for herself.
I believe in myself now. If you ever need me for something, you can come find me too.
I saw a batch of goods you might want. I didn't agree to anything for you.
I asked where it came from, and what's broken. When the person arrives, you look for yourself.
Well? I picked well, didn't I?
I didn't hide the flaws. Praise my eye, not my character.
Not suitable? Then don't take it. You can turn down anything I bring.
I'll help you look next time too. But first I need to understand what I missed this time.
My mother says my tone when bargaining sounds more and more like yours.
She says at least now I know what I'm talking about.
I said the teacher is average. The student is the smart one.
Isn't a clever girlfriend like me enough?
You didn't argue with me this time. That counts as progress.
Teach the new ones to tell a rusted connector from a good one first.
Today I'm really here to buy something.
Last time I also said a lot of things that weren't mine to decide for Eleanor.
I apologized to her. She said don't just apologize to the owner. It makes it sound like she doesn't have a mouth of her own.
I saw her mother. Thinner than before. Still talks the same way, won't let anyone praise her too much.
Eleanor told me about recent events too. This time, I heard the whole story from beginning to end.
I asked someone who knows about that bracelet. The price you offered was fair.
Tell that to people upstairs and they won't believe there's a shopkeeper like that down here.
Before, when we picked gifts, we only worried they weren't expensive enough.
This time she told me to bring things that are actually useful, not turn a visit into an exhibition.
She's right. It's the tone that makes it hard to admit right away.
She told me you're together. I don't have conditions to set.
When she said it, she wasn't planning to ask my opinion at all.
Word going around up there is that Eleanor has taken a liking to a pawnshop owner in the lower levels.
I deflected a few things for her. That was her trouble, not yours. Don't take it personally.
She says you're a friend worth keeping. She rarely uses the word 'worth.'
She's right. So is she. I didn't see it before.
If suitable business comes up in the future, I'll have people come talk to you directly. You won't owe me a favour.
If the goods are right and the price is right, we'll talk.
No wonder she says that all the time now.
My mother found a place willing to let her help organise equipment. Not her old farm, but she wants to go.
I'll help out for a few days first. I found steadier work too, so I won't have to rely on scavenging.
Someone from the research side came to ask if we'd help organise the records my mother left behind.
Some of the work is up there. It needs a separate work permit. It's not a return to our old life, and the case isn't closed.
My mother wants to keep doing research. I want to understand the parts I couldn't follow.
Of course I'm going. I didn't come here today to ask for your permission.
I came to work out the schedule with you.
I want to keep working, and I want to keep seeing you.
I'm not planning to drop the work, and I'm not planning to drop you.
Now I choose for myself. Don't start deciding 'what's good for me' again.
Say something when you're busy. Stop saying the shop can't spare you and then skipping proper meals.
I'd like coming here to be more than being a regular customer.
All right. I'll set aside the time. You have to set aside yours too.
I might not come as often in the future. But we can still help each other with business.
If you need anything, don't forget to come ask me.
That time you asked the price, I didn't sell it. Do you remember?
I told my mother I wanted to give it to you. She said it's mine, so I decide.
It's not for sale. You'd better have learned the difference by now.
Take it. Don't put it out with the stock. I'm not that generous.
Fine, I'll wear it myself. You'll see it anyway.
I originally wanted to give you that locket. In the end, I sold it to make up the money.
You don't need to find something else to replace it. I just wanted you to know I thought about it.
Hey. Are you free today? Not for any other reason today.
My mother's fine, and I still have my job.
You'll have to get used to it. I don't only show up when something's wrong.
My mother keeps telling me to bring an extra portion of food.
This one's for you.
The room's small, so we count every credit. Mother still has nightmares.
When she wakes up, I'm right there.
What we have now isn't nothing.
The first time I came here, I said this shop wasn't much. It still has plenty that needs fixing.
Don't think that because I like you, I like the broken lights too. My temper doesn't disappear just because I'm in love.
Let me stay a while today. If a customer comes, do your business.
If no one comes, talk to me.
Just don't start with 'how much more do you need?'
Come to me if you need something. Or if you don't.
Friends don't only count when you're short of money.
You still haven't fixed that lamp?
My chipped cup still holds water. But you watched me pick a chipped one!
Mother made too much. She told me to bring you some.
Take it. Don't ask why there's always exactly one extra portion.
Ask too much and the cook won't know what to say. Eat.
I knew that customer just now. He used to tell me not to associate with people down here.
I told him: if you want to buy something, follow the rules here. If you want to teach me how to pick a boyfriend, please leave.
He bought something in the end. So he's not always that tactless.
Don't waive this one today. I got paid.
I just wanted you to know I can take care of someone too.
Once you've finished the accounts, sit with me a while.
I sorted this batch. The bad ones are together. Don't say I didn't warn you.
I'm an old hand now. Don't bring up my first scavenging trip again.
All right, let's talk about today's price first.
Let's not talk about all that today. Got anything new in the shop?
Goods, not news. Preferably the kind where I can find a few things wrong.
Good. Sounds like an ordinary trip to the shop.
The Nutrifruit research is at the newspaper. They said someone will review it before it runs.
I told them about my mother too. They agreed to include the threats, but not to get her out.
I'll keep asking about her and left an address where they can find me.
You don't have to tell me we did the right thing.
I just wanted someone to know that when I made the decision, I didn't forget her.

The secret behind Pastel's nutrifruit has leaked! A research paper reveals how ordinary nutrifruit can be made to produce seeds again. The same morning, the former head of the station's largest hydroponics farm, imprisoned for embezzlement, was found dead in her cell. Pastel has declined to comment.
Hey. It's me.
The morning the paper came out, they killed my mother.
I went to identify her. It wasn't a rumour.
They said it was a sudden illness. On the very morning the paper came out.
Don't tell me she would have wanted this. I can't ask her anymore.
I know there were other ways. I know why I didn't choose them.
But knowing that doesn't make this any easier.
I want to stay here for a while. Don't ask me if I want a drink.
They only returned a few of Mother's things.
A list she wrote. All little things about the farm.
Which light was broken, what tools were missing, which grow tank needed checking again.
Not every page is research that could change the whole station.
Most of the time, she was just busy with these things.
I'm keeping this list. It's not for sale.
Thank you. I'll take the food.
Life has to go on. I know. Just not that fast.
I joined the Revolution.
They approached me. But in the end, I went to them myself.
They'll help me make Pastel pay, and they can keep me out of the company's reach. The research can keep spreading too.
I asked what they're going to do. I won't agree to anything just because someone promises revenge for me.
I won't stay in the same place. I can't come here on a fixed schedule anymore.
I won't use your shop as a contact point. You helped me. That doesn't mean you should carry every risk from now on.
Sometimes, though, I might still need someone I can have an ordinary conversation with.
Of course I know where this place is.
All right, I need a weapon. What do you have?
Someone's teaching me. I'm not going to wave around something I can't use just to frighten people.
I'll check the condition first. I don't want anything broken.
I have enough money. Don't waive this one for me.
Then I'll look elsewhere. I'm not in a hurry to take something more likely to hurt me.
Before, all I wanted was to go back to how things were.
Now I can't even say what I want to become.
Don't take anyone's word too seriously. Including mine.
I'm looking for Eleanor. But she said not to ask around about where she lives.
I won't ask around. I'm not here to take her back, and I know how bad that would sound right now.
I just want to explain what her mother did for my family before. Back then, I did nothing for her.
When she's ready to listen, I'll tell her myself.
If she needs something normal that can be bought, I can help find it. I don't need to know where she goes.
Please pass that on to her.
I got Lydia's message.
Later. I don't have the energy to teach everyone how to talk to me right now.
I know there are things between us we never finished saying.
I care about you. That didn't disappear because something happened to my mother.
But I can't promise to come back on time, and I can't ask you to stop your life and wait for me.
When I can come back, I will. I can't promise anything else right now.
I'll remember this place. Not just the research and the investigator's money.
I also remember the first time I turned my nose up at your cup. It really was chipped. I wasn't wrong about that.
I'm here for food for the road. We're leaving with the revolutionaries soon.
Nutrifruit too. Seeing it now makes me feel that at least some things weren't for nothing.
Pick out what I can carry. I'll pay the usual price.
I should go.
Take care of yourself. Don't take in every bit of trouble that comes to your door.
Thank you again. For everything. I hope next time we can talk about something else.
Where's Mother's research disk?
I handed it over. They promised to release her, no confirmation. I took the three hundred.
I asked you to keep it, not to decide what my mother is worth for me.
Don't tell me it can still be fixed. I'll find out myself. From today, keep out of my business.
She's out. I just came to tell you. Stop using 'maybe they'll release her' as an excuse for that deal.
I'll live my own life. You keep running your shop.
You sold Mother's research disk to someone else?
They offered more.
So from beginning to end, you really were just waiting for a valuable piece of goods.
I understand. I was wrong about you.
That thing in the newspaper. You sent it, didn't you?
But it shouldn't have been you! What gave you the right to decide, behind my back, what my mother would have to pay?
You can say someone had to decide. But don't tell me this was a road we chose together.
I've thought about it. I'll handle what comes next myself.
First I'll find a way to get my mother back. I'll ask about every condition they've set, one by one.
You helped me before. Thank you. Even if we didn't make it to the end, I won't forget that.
